title: Construction 6: Divide a segment into 2 or 3 equal parts without measuring
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: segment AB divided into three equal parts using a ray with equal steps, with arcs left visible

example.question: Divide the segment $[AB]$ into three equal parts using only a compass and straight edge. Show your construction lines.

steps.say: Start at $A$. Draw a ray from $A$ at any angle to $[AB]$. Make it fairly long.

rows.aside: With the straight edge, draw a ray from $A$ going up and to the right.

steps.say: Set the compass to any small width. Do not change it again.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $A$, draw an arc across the ray. Call the crossing $1$.
Move the point to $1$ and, keeping the same width, draw another arc. Call the crossing $2$.
Move the point to $2$, same width, and mark $3$.

steps.say: The three arcs are equal. Join $3$ to $B$.

rows.aside: With the straight edge, draw the line from $3$ to $B$.

steps.say: Copy the angle at $3$ to the points $2$ and $1$, so each new line is parallel to $[3B]$.

rows.aside: Through $2$, draw a line parallel to $[3B]$. It meets $[AB]$ at $Q$.
Through $1$, draw a line parallel to $[3B]$. It meets $[AB]$ at $P$.
Then $|AP| = |PQ| = |QB|$. Leave all arcs and lines showing.

issues: Only the ray point 3 is labelled. The working says to call the crossings 1 and 2, but those two points have no labels.
No compass arcs are shown although the working says to leave all arcs showing.

title: Construction 18: Angle of 60° without protractor or set square
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: 60° angle at A from an equilateral-triangle arc, with arcs left visible

example.question: Using only a compass and straight edge, construct an angle of $60^\circ$ at the point $A$ on the line $[AB]$.

steps.say: Open the compass to the length $|AB|$. Keep it this width for the whole construction.

rows.aside: Place the compass point on $A$ and the pencil on $B$.

steps.say: The point $C$ must be $|AB|$ from $A$, so it lies on an arc centred at $A$.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $A$, draw a long arc above the line.

steps.say: The point $C$ must also be $|AB|$ from $B$. The two arcs cross at $C$.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $B$, same width, draw an arc that crosses the first. Call the crossing $C$.
With the straight edge, draw $[AC]$.
Every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$, so $|\angle BAC| = 60^\circ$.
Leave both arcs showing.

issues: The label C sits on top of the two crossing arcs and is partly struck through.
The second arc (centre B) is only a tiny stub near C, so the construction lines the working describes are hard to see.

title: Construction 20: Parallelogram given side lengths and angles
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: parallelogram with AB 6, AD 4 and angle 70°, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the parallelogram $ABCD$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|AD| = 4$ cm and $|\angle DAB| = 70^\circ$.

steps.say: Start with the side you are given first. Draw it on the horizontal so the angle is easy to measure.

rows.aside: With the ruler, draw $[AB]$ of length $6$ cm.

steps.say: The angle sits at $A$, between $[AB]$ and $[AD]$.

rows.aside: Put the protractor centre on $A$ with its base along $[AB]$.
Mark $70^\circ$ and draw a ray from $A$ through the mark.

steps.say: $D$ is on that ray, $4$ cm from $A$.

rows.aside: With the ruler, measure $4$ cm along the ray from $A$. Label it $D$.

steps.say: Opposite sides are equal, so $|BC| = 4$ cm and $|DC| = 6$ cm.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $B$, open to $4$ cm and draw an arc.
With the compass point on $D$, open to $6$ cm and draw an arc that crosses it. Label the crossing $C$.
Draw $[BC]$, $[CD]$. Label every corner and leave the arcs showing.

issues: Sides are not in proportion: AB is 6 cm but AD and BC (4 cm) are drawn about half the length of AB, not two thirds. The height is also too small for 4 sin 70 against 6.
No compass arcs are shown although the working says to leave the arcs showing.

title: Construction 16: Circumcentre and circumcircle of a triangle (straight edge and compass)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with its three perpendicular bisectors meeting at the circumcentre and the circumcircle, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the circumcentre and circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 7$ cm, $|BC| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Use a compass and straight edge and show your construction lines.
example.final: O\text{ is where the perpendicular bisectors meet; circle with centre }O\text{ through }A,B,C

steps.say: Draw the longest side first, then find the third corner with two arcs.

rows.aside: Draw $[AB]$ of length $7$ cm.
From $A$, draw an arc of radius $5$ cm. From $B$, draw an arc of radius $6$ cm. Label the crossing $C$ and join up the triangle.

steps.say: The circumcentre is the same distance from $A$ and $B$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

rows.aside: Open the compass past half of $|AB|$. Draw an arc above and below $[AB]$ from $A$, then from $B$ with the same width.
Join the two crossings with the straight edge.

steps.say: It is also the same distance from $A$ and $C$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AC]$.

rows.aside: Repeat the construction on $[AC]$.
The two bisectors cross. Label that point $O$.

steps.say: $O$ is the same distance from all three corners.

rows.aside: Put the compass point on $O$ and the pencil on $A$.
Draw the circle. It passes through $A$, $B$ and $C$. Leave all arcs showing.

issues: The triangle does not match the lengths: with AB = 7, AC should be about 5/7 of AB and BC about 6/7, but the drawn AC is about 0.89 of AB and BC about 1.02. C is too high and too far left.
The label O is overlapped by the bisector lines through it.
No construction arcs are shown for the bisectors or for locating C, although the working says to leave all arcs showing.
